name: Beef Bulgogi (Korean Fire Beef)
why: Korean BBQ's most iconic dish at home: ribeye thinly sliced, soaked in a baking-soda tenderiser, marinated in a blended soy-sugar-ginger-garlic sauce, then seared hard in a screaming-hot pan until it caramelises glossy. Big flavour in under 10 minutes of actual cooking time.
author: Henry
ingredients: 1 1/2 tbsp vegetable oil, plus 2 tsp for cooking
1 tbsp roughly chopped fresh ginger (from a 1-inch knob)
1/4 tsp crushed red pepper flakes, heaped
2 scallions, dark green parts only, thinly sliced, to serve

steps: Place the steaks on a large plate and freeze for about 35 minutes until semi-firm — this makes them far easier to slice. Slice across the grain into 1/4-inch (6mm) thick slices.
Combine 1 1/2 tablespoons of water with the baking soda in a medium bowl. Add the beef slices and toss to coat. Leave to sit at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, in a mini food processor or blender, combine the 1 1/2 tablespoons vegetable oil, sesame oil, soy sauce, brown sugar, garlic, shallot, ginger and red pepper flakes. Process until smooth.
Pour the marinade over the beef and toss to coat evenly. Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour (or overnight for maximum flavour).
Turn on the exhaust fan — it gets smoky. Heat the remaining 2 teaspoons of vegetable oil in a large 12-inch (30cm) cast iron or nonstick skillet over medium-high heat until very hot and shimmering.
Add half the beef in a single layer and cook without stirring until browned and caramelised on one side, 2-3 minutes.
Stir the meat and continue stir-frying until just cooked through, 1-2 minutes longer. Transfer to a serving platter and cover to keep warm.
Add the remaining beef to the same pan (no more oil) along with any marinade left in the bowl. Cook 2-3 minutes until browned on one side, then stir-fry 1-2 minutes more until just cooked through.
Transfer the second batch to the platter and sprinkle with the scallion greens and sesame seeds.
Serve immediately over steamed white rice — the pan juices are worth spooning over the rice.

pro_tips: The baking soda soak is the secret weapon — it tenderises the beef and helps the soy-sugar marinade caramelise properly in the pan. If you're sensitive to its slight soapy taste, give the meat a quick rinse before marinating.
The 35-minute freeze step is what makes this work at home: semi-firm beef slices into wafer-thin pieces that sear evenly instead of steaming. Never skip it.
